name: favourited-row-becomes-its-tile-and-leaves-with-it
description:
A favourite tile is a tab in another shape. Dropping a tab row on the favourites grid used to add a tile and leave the row, so the page showed twice. Now the new tile claims the row's tab: the row goes, the tile is selected because that tab is the one on screen, and Remove from Favorites closes the tab with the tile, so no page is left open with nothing in the sidebar to reach it.

The fixture's Dark space holds one favourite on a slow page and one tab on example-domain.html, which is no favourite. The scenario sends the same messages the drop and the context menu send.

actions.expression: (() => { const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('.railpane:not(.ovrailpane) .row.tabrow')]; return rows.length + ' rows ' + document.querySelectorAll('.fav').length + ' tiles ' + document.querySelectorAll('.fav.sel').length + ' selected'; })()
actions.note: one row, the example page, and one tile, the slow favourite

actions.expression: (() => { const r = document.querySelector('.railpane:not(.ovrailpane) .row.tabrow'); if (!r) return 'no-row'; r.click(); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: the row's tab on screen, so the tile that takes it over is the selected one
what a drop of the row on the favourites grid sends

actions.expression: (() => { const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('.railpane:not(.ovrailpane) .row.tabrow')]; return rows.length + ' rows ' + document.querySelectorAll('.fav').length + ' tiles ' + document.querySelectorAll('.fav.sel').length + ' selected'; })()
(() => { const t = document.querySelector('.fav.sel'); if (!t) return 'no-tile'; chrome.send('sidebarFavoriteRemoved', [t.dataset.favId]); return 'sent ' + t.dataset.favId; })()
actions.note: the context menu's Remove from Favorites

actions.expression: (() => { const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('.railpane:not(.ovrailpane) .row.tabrow')]; return rows.length + ' rows ' + document.querySelectorAll('.fav').length + ' tiles ' + document.querySelectorAll('.fav.sel').length + ' selected'; })()
actions.note: the new tile is gone and no row came back: the tab closed with the tile

actions.pattern: Atrium: favourite removed - closing its tab

assertions.desc: the control: one row, three tiles, before any gesture
AC: the row became the tile. The tile holds the tab, so it is the selected one and the row is gone.
AC: removing the favourite closed its tab, so nothing came back as a row

assertions.pattern: Atrium: favourited row claims its tab
assertions.desc: the drop claimed the row's tab for the tile
